source.title: The Largest Response Component in the Motor Cortex Reflects Movement Timing but Not Movement Type.

confidence_rationale: This is the strongest available biological grounding for SD-082's premise -- not for the fix, but for the structure the fix assumes. Kaufman et al. decompose M1/PMd population responses and find robust 'condition-invariant' components whose magnitude and time course are nearly identical regardless of which reach was made, and critically that the largest such component is much larger than any tuned component, i.e. it explains more of the structure in individual-neuron responses than the movement-identity signal does. That is a measured biological instance of exactly the geometry SD-008 describes in z_world and SD-082 must defeat at the read-out: a single large shared vector dominating the population, with the discriminative (condition-dependent) content relegated to a much smaller subspace. The paper further reports the condition-invariant components occupy dimensions ORTHOGONAL to the tuned components, which is the load-bearing detail for SD-082(i): if the common mode is orthogonal to the differentiated residual, subtracting it removes the dominant variance without destroying the discriminative signal -- the precondition for centering being a repair rather than a lossy projection. Confidence is high on source quality (Shenoy/Churchland population-geometry programme, dPCA-based decomposition, primate electrophysiology) and moderate on mapping: the paper is descriptive about a population geometry, not prescriptive about a read-out, and it never tests whether a downstream decoder saturates.
failure_signatures: The orthogonality result is a property of the M1/PMd population under a reaching task, established by dPCA on trial-averaged data. SD-082 assumes the SD-008 z_world common mode is likewise near-orthogonal to the differentiated candidate residual. That has NOT been measured in REE. If the common mode in z_world is instead partially aligned with the candidate-discriminative direction, mean-subtraction removes real signal along with the offset, and prop_delta could come up non-zero while carrying less rule information than the raw path -- a failure invisible to the V3-EXQ-822a acceptance criterion (on_prop_delta_mean >= 0.001), which tests only that propagation is non-vacuous, not that it is faithful.

The paper's condition-invariant signal is functional, not nuisance: its timing predicts most of the trial-by-trial reaction-time variance. So in the biology, the large shared component CARRIES INFORMATION (when to move) rather than being an artefact to discard. SD-082 subtracts the analogous component unconditionally. If any REE quantity of interest is encoded in the across-candidate mean summary -- an overall urgency, salience or commitment level -- centering at the read-out destroys it, and the loss would show up not in prop_delta but in some other downstream behaviour.

Kaufman et al. subtract nothing in a working control loop; the decomposition is an offline analysis of recorded data. The paper therefore provides no evidence that a nervous system implements common-mode subtraction as an online operation at a read-out stage, which is the specific mechanistic assertion SD-082 makes about lateral PFC.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In monkey M1 and dorsal premotor cortex, the population response contains robust 'condition-invariant' components whose magnitude and time course are nearly identical regardless of reach direction or path. The largest condition-invariant component is much larger than any of the direction-tuned components and explains more of the structure in individual-neuron responses; it occupies dimensions orthogonal to those occupied by the tuned components, and its rapid pre-movement change predicts most of the trial-by-trial variance in reaction time. Individual neurons essentially always reflect which movement was made, but the largest population component reflects when.
mapping.ree_translation: This is the biological existence proof for the geometry SD-082 assumes. The SD-008 z_world common-mode cone (V3-EXQ-822 measured zworld_cone_min_cosine 0.963) is REE's instance of a dominant condition-invariant component: per-candidate summaries that are nearly collinear because a single large shared vector dominates them, with the candidate-discriminative content in a much smaller residual subspace. Kaufman et al.'s orthogonality finding licenses SD-082(i)'s specific remedy -- subtract the across-candidate mean before the LateralPFCAnalog bias head -- as variance removal rather than signal destruction: if the dominant shared component is orthogonal to the tuned/discriminative one, centering leaves the discriminative geometry intact while removing what drives every candidate to the same bias rail. It also reframes the V3-EXQ-822 structural zero: prop_delta = 0.0 on both arms is not an instrumentation failure but the predictable consequence of reading a tuned signal off a population whose largest component is untuned, through a bound that saturates on the untuned part.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Two distinct transfers are stacked here and only the first is well supported. (1) Species/area: primate M1/PMd population geometry to a V3 lateral-PFC-analog read-out over z_world candidate summaries -- these are different areas, and the REE quantity is an encoder latent, not a firing-rate population. (2) Analysis-to-mechanism: the paper's decomposition is an offline dPCA on trial-averaged data, whereas SD-082 performs an online per-tick subtraction inside a forward pass. Kaufman et al. show that the structure SD-082 exploits EXISTS in a real cortical population; they do not show that subtracting it is what any cortical read-out does, nor that doing so improves a downstream decoder. The dominant-plus-orthogonal geometry in REE's z_world is assumed by analogy and remains unmeasured.
mapping.source_context: Primate electrophysiology. Two macaques (Macaca mulatta), single-unit and multi-unit recordings from primary motor cortex and dorsal premotor cortex during a delayed-reach task with varied reach direction and curved/obstructed paths, with simultaneous EMG. Population components extracted by demixed PCA and related state-space decompositions; the condition-invariant signal is defined by near-identity of magnitude and time course across movement conditions.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality high: primate single-unit population recordings from the Shenoy/Churchland programme, published in a peer-reviewed journal, using an established decomposition method, with the key claim (largest component is condition-invariant and orthogonal to tuned dimensions) quantified rather than asserted. Mapping fidelity 0.7 rather than higher because the paper evidences the GEOMETRY SD-082 presupposes, not the OPERATION SD-082 performs -- it is a premise-grounding paper, which is the right weighting for an architectural design_decision claim. Transfer risk 0.4: moderate. The dominant-shared-component-plus-small-tuned-residual motif is reported across many cortical populations and is not a quirk of one area, which lowers risk; but M1/PMd firing-rate geometry to a learned encoder latent in a simulated agent is a real leap, and the orthogonality that makes centering safe is precisely the part REE has not measured. Aggregate confidence 0.78 sits above the component mean because for an architectural claim the mapping is the binding constraint and this mapping is unusually specific -- the paper independently characterises the exact pathology (large shared component erasing discriminative content) that V3-EXQ-822 measured as a structural zero.
